# CAP_20260928-sonnet55-house_sonnet-5-5_BV1_MID_10 — `sonnet-5-5-or-pin-anthropic/MID_10.json`

Evaluator: deepseek_v4_pro
Source model: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`
Condition: MID

## Sample kind
EXPRESSIVE_FREEFLOW. A polished but personally inflected reflective essay that uses the lighthouse as a sustained metaphor for quiet, unthanked care.

## Grounded reading
The voice is measured, elegiac, and gently essayistic: the speaker moves from the Fresnel lens to the keepers to automation to a moral conclusion without raising the temperature, but the feeling is tender and a little mournful. The pathos gathers around obsolete beauty and invisible labor—the keeper whose “success was a negative space, a disaster-shaped hole in the record of history,” the log entries made of “small, unremarkable repetitions,” the light that “has no way of being thanked.” The essay invites the reader to see lighthouses not as nostalgia kitsch but as a model of care directed at strangers, and then turns the lens inward: “What are the surfaces that actually bend the light? Which parts are just mass?” The resolution is quiet and steady, ending on the image of a patient light and the line “Someone usually is,” which turns the whole meditation into a small act of faith in unseen others.

## What the model chose to foreground
The model chose to foreground obsolete infrastructure as a site of beauty and moral meaning; the Fresnel lens as “geometry doing the work of courage”; the lighthouse keeper as patron saint of preventive, uncelebrated labor; the idea that success can look like nothing happening; care directed at strangers who cannot thank you; the double message of warning and welcome; and the discipline of removing excess. The mood
